A Taddhita affix of the comparative degree, added to adjectives,
 nouns, and also to verbs and indeclinables in which latter case it is
 changed to तराम्. It is added, like तम, to pronouns in the sense
 of ‘one of two’ e. g. कतर, ततर, यतर &c.

——(a) N. of the wife of Vāli, king of the monkeys, and mother of Aṅgada.
 She in vain tried to dissuade her husband Vāli from fighting with Rāma
 and Sugrīva, and married Sugrīva after Vāli had been killed by Rāma.
——(b) N. of the wife of Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of the gods. She
 was on one occasion carried off by Soma (the moon) who refused to deliver
 her up to her husband when demanded. A fierce contest then ensued, and
 Brahmā had at last to compel Soma to restore her to her husband. Tārā
 gave birth to a son named Budha who became the ancestor of the Lunar race
 of kings (see

).
——(c) N. of the wife of Hariśchandra and mother of Rohidāsa (also
 called Tārāmatī).
——(d) N. of a Buddha goddess.
——(e) N. of a Śakti; Jaina.

N. of a demon killed by Kārtikeya. [He was the son of Vajrāṅga
 and Varāṅgī. He propitiated the god Brahmadeva by means of his penance

 killed by any one except a child seven days old. On the strength of this
 boon he began to oppress the gods who were obliged to go to Brahmā and
 ask his assistance in the destruction of the demon (see

 were told that the offspring of Śiva could alone vanquish him. Afterwards
 Kārtikeya was born, and he slew the demon on the seventh day of his birth].
